record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Maximizers of V_min times Euler number
record.original_question: For reflexive polytopes, is the maximum of the product V_{n,min} chi attained by fibrations of dP_3, possibly in more than one way?

evidence.quote: Question 14. Is the maximum value for Vn,minχ for reflexive polytopes attained by various (not necessarily uniquely) dP3 fibrations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A lattice polytope $\Delta \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing the origin in its interior is called reflexive if its polar dual $\Delta^\circ = \{u \in \mathbb{R}^n : \langle u, v\rangle \ge -1 \text{ for all } v \in \Delta\}$ is also a lattice polytope. Each reflexive polytope $\Delta$ determines a Gorenstein toric Fano variety $X_\Delta$ and a corresponding affine toric Calabi–Yau cone $C(Y_\Delta)$ of complex dimension $n+1$ over a Sasaki–Einstein base $Y_\Delta$. Let $V_{n,\min}(\Delta)$ denote the minimum value, taken over Reeb vectors compatible with the toric structure, of the volume function of the Sasaki–Einstein base $Y_\Delta$ (equivalently, the volume minimized via $Z$-minimization over the cone of admissible Reeb vectors associated to $\Delta$), normalized so that $V_{n,\min}$ equals the volume of the round unit sphere $S^{2n+1}$ for the trivial cone. Let $\chi(\Delta)$ denote the Euler number of a smooth crepant resolution of $X_\Delta$ (equivalently, the number of lattice points on the boundary of $\Delta$ minus the appropriate corrections, computed combinatorially from $\Delta$).

Among reflexive polytopes one distinguishes those whose corresponding toric variety admits the structure of a fibration whose generic fiber is the del Pezzo surface $dP_3$ (the blowup of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at three points in general position), realized at the level of polytopes by a projection of $\Delta$ onto a lower-dimensional reflexive polytope whose fibers are the reflexive hexagon associated with $dP_3$.

Question. For each fixed $n$, consider the product $V_{n,\min}(\Delta)\, \chi(\Delta)$ as $\Delta$ ranges over all $n$-dimensional reflexive polytopes. Is the maximum of this product attained by reflexive polytopes corresponding to $dP_3$ fibrations, possibly by more than one such fibration (i.e., not necessarily uniquely)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions in quiver gauge theory. A web search did not turn up a subsequent resolution; related work on Calabi–Yau volumes and reflexive polytopes (e.g. the paper "Calabi–Yau Volumes and Reflexive Polytopes" and follow-ups on quiver gauge theories beyond reflexivity) discusses bounds and patterns for $V_{\min}\cdot\chi$ but does not appear to settle the question. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Calabi–Yau Volumes and Reflexive Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimized Sasaki–Einstein volumes for Calabi–Yau cones from reflexive polytopes and conjectures bounds involving Euler characteristics.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework of $V_{n,\min}$ and conjectures relating it to topological invariants, but does not resolve the maximum-attainment question for $dP_3$ fibrations.

status_evidence.title: Quiver gauge theories: beyond reflexivity (JHEP 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the analysis of toric Calabi–Yau volumes beyond reflexive polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work in the area but does not record a proof or disproof of this specific extremality question.
